identity.title: Data Selection via Optimal Control for Language Models

problem.claim: Select high-quality pre-training data from massive corpora to improve language-model capabilities on downstream tasks.

contributions.claim: Formulates data selection as generalized optimal control, derives PMP necessary conditions for optimal selection and training dynamics, and introduces PDS to approximate those conditions.
Applies PDS to CommonCrawl data selection and reports benefits across model sizes, including improved data utilization under limited pre-training data.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors present PMP-based Data Selection (PDS), derived from an optimal-control formulation of data selection.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that PDS-selected corpora accelerate language-model learning and consistently improve downstream performance across various model sizes and tasks.
The authors report that Scaling-Law extrapolation of test-loss curves indicates benefits extending to approximately 400B-parameter models trained on approximately 10T tokens.
With limited pre-training data, the authors report a 1.8× reduction in data demand, helping delay exhaustion of web-crawled corpora.

narrative_sequence.summary: The work targets high-quality pre-training data selection from massive corpora for downstream language-model capability.
Data selection is cast as generalized optimal control, with PMP supplying necessary conditions linking selection to training dynamics.
PDS is introduced as an approximation that solves the PMP conditions.
CommonCrawl experiments report faster learning, broad downstream gains, scaling-law-based projected benefits for very large models, lower data demand, and public code, models, and data.

source_observation.claim: The abstract connects a theoretical formulation and necessary conditions directly to an operational data-selection framework, then reports effects at multiple model scales and data regimes.

lessons.interpretation: A compact theory-to-method-to-scope narrative can make a proposed intervention and its claimed applicability easier to assess.
lessons.application: When presenting a new selection or optimization method, state the governing conditions, the approximation used in practice, and the distinct regimes in which evidence is reported.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when the method has no meaningful theoretical characterization or when the available evaluation does not cover the claimed regimes.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify baselines, quantitative downstream gains, statistical variation, or details of the PMP approximation.
The approximately 400B-model claim is based on test-loss-curve extrapolation via Scaling Laws rather than reported direct training at that scale.
The basis and scope of the reported 1.8× data-demand reduction are not detailed.
